record.original_question: Let E^2 denote the Euclidean plane. A set X is monochromatic in a coloring if all points of a congruent copy of X receive the same color. For every non-equilateral triangle T, viewed as the set of its three vertices, must every 2-coloring of E^2 contain a monochromatic congruent copy of T?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{E}^2$ denote the Euclidean plane. Given a finite set $X \subset \mathbb{E}^2$ and a coloring $c: \mathbb{E}^2 \to \{1,2\}$, say that $X$ is monochromatic (under $c$) if there exists a congruent copy $X'$ of $X$ in $\mathbb{E}^2$ such that all points of $X'$ receive the same color. A triangle $T$ is identified with the 3-point set of its vertices, and is called non-equilateral if its three side lengths are not all equal.

Prove or disprove: for every non-equilateral triangle $T \subset \mathbb{E}^2$ and every 2-coloring $c : \mathbb{E}^2 \to \{1,2\}$, there is a monochromatic congruent copy of $T$.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture (due to Erdős, Graham, Montgomery, Rothschild, Spencer, and Straus) remains open in general. It has been verified for several special families of triangles (e.g., right triangles, isosceles triangles with specific ratios, and—established more recently—all 3-term arithmetic progressions, i.e., degenerate triangles whose vertices are collinear and equally spaced). No counterexample is known, but a complete proof for arbitrary non-equilateral triangles has not been established.

status_evidence.snippet: Erdős, Graham, Montgomery, Rothschild, Spencer, Straus conjectured that any 2-coloring of the plane contains a monochromatic congruent copy of every non-equilateral triangle; verified for special classes.
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture stated and known only for special families.

status_evidence.title: Any two-coloring of the plane contains monochromatic 3-term arithmetic progressions
status_evidence.snippet: Confirms a natural case of the conjecture: every 2-coloring of E^2 has a monochromatic congruent copy of any 3-term AP.
status_evidence.claim: Recent partial progress on the conjecture.
